newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy says Mideast mission aims at security.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy says Mideast mission aims at security.

text.p: U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross said on Sunday his peace-saving mission aimed to restore Israeli-Palestinian security cooperation.

"A security relationship has to be established in a way that is productive and effective and that's really the purpose of my efforts right now," he told reporters after meeting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

U.S. President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright sent Ross to the region late on Saturday to try to ease Israeli-PLO tensions plunged deeper into crisis by a suicide bombing in a Jerusalem marketplace, killing 15 people.

"The president and the secretary want me to focus on the security questions and I will be doing that and we will be seeing what we can do to try to put things back together again in that respect," Ross said.
"The president and the secretary of state are committed to doing all they can to help the parties to put the (peace) process back together again.

"They recognise that there is a political dimension that has to be addressed but they also understand that there is an essential security underpinning to the process," Ross said before heading to the West Bank town of Ramallah to meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
